newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister says government mulling polls.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says government mulling polls.

text.p: A Turkish cabinet minister said on Tuesday the Islamist-led coalition was discussing elections as a way to clear up a crisis over Moslem activism which has eroded the government's hold on power.
"Elections are on the agenda. That is what we are debating," State Minister Salim Ensarioglu told reporters before ministers gathered for the first cabinet meeting in eight weeks.

The possibility of early polls has increasingly been raised since Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition began to buckle under the weight of pressure by the secularist armed forces for an anti-Islamist crackdown.

"The date is not certain," Ensarioglu, who belongs to the conservative True Path Party led by Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, said when asked about the timing of any early polls. The next general elections must be held by the year 2000.
After the cabinet meeting, which lasted just under three hours, a government spokesman held out the possibility of elections in comments to reporters.
"Without doubt when it is necessary going to the country is the most unavoidable path," Islamist State Minister Abdullah Gul said in answer to a reporter's question.

He said the meeting focused on army demands for a crackdown on Islamist activism. The demands have created a deepening rift between Islamist leader Erbakan and the pro-Western True Path and forced the cancellation of recent cabinet meetings.
Three True Path ministers have resigned in the last month. The government needs a simple majority in parliament to call early elections, favoured by some of the opposition.
The coalition partners are deadlocked over an army-backed plan to restrict religious education as part of a secularist campaign to erode support for Erbakan's Welfare Party.

A top prosecutor has opened a case at the constitutional court aimed at closing the Islam-based party for undermining the secular state. Erbakan responded on Tuesday by seeking damages of 20 billion lira ($140,000) from the prosecutor, Anatolian news agency reported.
Erbakan's lawyers were not immediately available for comment and his office said it had no information on the case.
Newspapers said on Tuesday Erbakan had backed an army plan to sack scores of Islamist soldiers after months of military pressure.
The Milliyet daily said Erbakan signed documents approving the dishonourable discharge of 161 officers and non-commissioned officers at a meeting of the Supreme Military Council on Monday.
"Ninety percent of the expulsions were for fundamentalism and the rest for extreme leftist activities," the paper said.
Other papers carried similar reports from the six-hour closed-door meeting of the Supreme Military Council, grouping the secularist top generals and the prime minister.
Four anti-Islamist MPs from the True Path Party have resigned in recent days, reducing the government's majority on paper to one. However, vacant seats give it a larger margin.

Milliyet said the generals warned that the small Islamist press was attacking secularists and setting them up as targets for Islamist violence, the paper said. "They gave Erbakan a caution about these publications," it said.
